fall_president.name: Jim Haynes
fall_president.evidence: Associated Students Leaders Do Well: Lack Communication

note: No Herald headline in either term names the sitting president outright. The fall item reviews Associated Students leadership without naming anyone; the February 1967 item names Haynes in a student government context during the spring election season. Nothing in the 1966-67 article index carries resignation, impeachment, acting or interim language, and the Herald's own year-end review of 12 May 1967 treats the year as a single administration.

fall_president.name: William Menser
fall_president.evidence: Dr. Kelly Thompson, William Menser Welcome Students

note: Menser opened the year alongside President Kelly Thompson and was still speaking as the outgoing officer in the issue that covered the race to replace him. The Herald of 4 April 1968 reported that he took up the Board of Regents seat, but he did not leave the presidency: he appears in the 29 April 1968 issue as the sitting officer. No fill-in was needed.

fall_president.name: Bill Straeffer
fall_president.evidence: Kelly Thompson, Bill Straeffer Welcome Students

spring_president.name: Bill Straeffer
spring_president.evidence: Bill Straeffer, Terry Gilpin Review Their Year with Associated Students

note: Straeffer opened the year with President Thompson and closed it reviewing his term with vice president Terry Gilpin. The plaque's separate 'Reed Morgan 1968' plate is not a mid-year presidency: a full sweep of the digitised archive finds Reed Morgan only in spring 1966, as a graduating senior who chaired the committee that drafted the Associated Students constitution. He does not appear anywhere in 1968.

fall_president.name: Larry Zielke
fall_president.evidence: Zielke, Lawrence & David Porter. Associated Student Government Replies

spring_president.name: Larry Zielke
spring_president.evidence: Larry Zielke Continues to Work on Teacher Evaluation

note: The fall item is a joint reply signed by Zielke and vice president David Porter, which fixes both officers in post. No headline between January and May 1970 names the president; the 28 April 1970 piece is headed only 'Associated Students President Predicts New Breed Leaders'. Zielke was still running the teacher-evaluation project in the summer issue. No succession language appears anywhere in the year.

spring_president.name: John Lyne
spring_president.evidence: Lyne, John. Says Associated Student Lectures Attacked

note: Lyne appears as the acting head of the organisation in both terms, including a January 1971 letter about an appointment he said he was kept in the dark about. He faced a criminal charge in September 1970 after police broke up a party, but the case was dismissed on 25 September and he stayed in office.

fall_president.name: Linda Jones
fall_president.evidence: Jones, Linda. Corrects College Heights Herald

spring_president.name: Linda Jones
spring_president.evidence: Linda Jones Looks Back on Past Year

note: Jones corrected the Herald on the organisation's behalf in both terms, in October 1971 and again in February 1972, and the paper ran a look-back interview with her in April 1972 in the issue that installed her successors.

fall_president.name: Edward Jordan, Jr.
fall_president.evidence: Associated Student Government Vice President is Anti-Apathy

note: No Herald headline in 1972-73 calls Jordan president; the identification rests on his April 1972 election, on the 1973 Talisman caption already cited in this archive, and on the September 1972 profile that fixes Michael Fiorella as the vice president rather than the president. Jordan wrote to the paper in both terms. Nothing in the year carries resignation, impeachment or acting language.

fall_president.name: Steven Yater
fall_president.evidence: press release featuring Steve Yater, president of the Student Government Association

src.label: WKU Archives UA11/2 press release, 11 Oct 1973

spring_president.name: Steven Yater
spring_president.evidence: Associated Student Government President Yater Defends His Administration in Letter

note: The university's own October 1973 press release names Yater as president in the fall term, and the Herald printed his defence of his administration in April 1974, a week before its retrospective headed 'Presidency Ends for Steve Yater'.

fall_president.name: Jeffrey Consolo
fall_president.evidence: Jeff Consolo Tabs Eight for Congress

spring_president.name: Jeffrey Consolo
spring_president.evidence: Jeff Consolo Notes Progress in His Term

note: Consolo was making presidential appointments to the congress in September 1974 and speaking for the organisation in February and April 1975. Three vacant congress seats were filled in January 1975, but those were congress seats, not the presidency.

fall_president.name: Steve Henry
fall_president.evidence: Steve Henry Says Hours for Women May End

spring_president.name: Steve Henry
spring_president.evidence: Steve Henry's Role Required Balancing Regent Associated Student Government Jobs

note: Henry spoke for the organisation through both terms and the Herald's closing assessment described him balancing the regent seat against the presidency. The impeachment case that ran through spring 1976 was against Gerard Faulk, head of the Judicial Council, who was acquitted on 9 April 1976; it never touched the presidency.

fall_president.name: Christy Mollozzi
fall_president.evidence: Vogt, Christy. Associated Student Government President Offers Explanations

spring_president.name: Christy Mollozzi
spring_president.evidence: Christy Vogt Sees Associated Student Government Differently

note: She held the office under the name Christy Vogt, which is how the Herald printed it throughout; the plaque records Christy Mollozzi. Her byline as president runs from the first fall issues to her closing piece of 29 April 1977.

fall_president.name: Robert Moore
fall_president.evidence: A$G? Bob Moore Questions Spending by Freshmen Candidates

spring_president.name: Robert Moore
spring_president.evidence: no spring headline names the president

note: Moore is named as the sitting president in October 1977, but no Herald headline between January and May 1978 names the president at all, so the spring term rests on the absence of any change rather than on a positive identification. The vacancy that year was in the vice presidency: Brent Shockley quit the post on 29 September 1977 and David Bass became vice president on 1 December 1977.

fall_president.name: Steven Thornton
fall_president.evidence: Associated Student Government Backs Thornton's Plan to Add Minorities to Panel

spring_president.name: Steven Thornton
spring_president.evidence: Thornton, Steve & Bob Moore. Endorses Candidates

note: The congress backed Thornton's own proposal in October 1978, and in March 1979 he was elected to the executive council of the Student Government Association of Kentucky, a seat held by campus presidents. The 1 May 1979 piece headed 'Associated Student Government President Wants More Student Involvement' does not print a name, so the spring identification is inferential.

fall_president.name: James Hargroave
fall_president.evidence: Associated Student Government Head Believes Students Interested

spring_president.name: James Hargroave
spring_president.evidence: Jamie Hargrove Says Associated Student Government has Laid Foundations

note: The Herald spells the name Jamie Hargrove in both terms; the plaque reads HARGROAVE and that discrepancy is already flagged in this archive. A letter headed 'Resignation Clarified' ran on 6 November 1979, but it sits in the letters column and the president was still in post in January 1980, so it did not concern the presidency.

fall_president.name: Steven Fuller
fall_president.evidence: Associated Student Government's Low Attendance Disappoints President

spring_president.name: Steven Fuller
spring_president.evidence: no spring headline names the president

note: Fuller is named as president in the October 1980 report on poor attendance. No headline between January and April 1981 names the president, so the spring term rests on the absence of any change. The next administration was sworn in on 16 April 1981 after Marcel Bush beat David Sturgeon in the regular April election.

fall_president.name: Marcell Bush
fall_president.evidence: Marcel Bush Wants Students to Understand Associated Student Government

spring_president.name: David Payne
spring_president.evidence: Associated Student Government President Marcel Bush Resigns

new_people.name: David Payne
new_people.how: Succeeded Marcel Bush, who resigned the presidency on 14 January 1982.
new_people.note: Already recorded in this archive and not re-researched. The Herald reported Bush's resignation on 14 January 1982 and Payne carried the office through the balance of the term, appearing as the organisation's spokesman in the paper from 19 January onward. Board of Regents minutes of 30 January 1982 name him as president.

note: This is the only presidential resignation the digitised record shows between 1966 and 1985. It was already in the archive before this pass.

fall_president.name: Margaret Ragan
fall_president.evidence: Major ASG Changes are Envisioned by Margaret Ragan

spring_president.name: Margaret Ragan
spring_president.evidence: Margaret Ragan to Tackle Tough Issues

note: Ragan opened the year with a plan for the organisation and opened the spring semester the same way. Her own piece of 3 February 1983 set out that the presidency and the student regent seat were separate offices.

spring_president.name: Jack Smith
spring_president.evidence: Top Associated Student Government Officers Seek Re-Election

note: Smith wrote for the organisation in September and December 1983 and was the subject of letters for and against him through the fall. He and the other top officers stood for re-election in February 1984 and the top four posts were settled on 20 March 1984. The vacancy that year was in the vice presidency: William Chandler quit on 12 January 1984 and three replacements were nominated a week later.

fall_president.name: Jack Smith
fall_president.evidence: Jack Smith: Associated Student Government Emperor

spring_president.name: Jack Smith
spring_president.evidence: Jack Smith Ends Term as Associated Student Government President

note: Smith served a second year and the Herald marked the end of his term on 11 April 1985, a week after reporting that Mitchell McKinney had been elected to succeed him. The Associated Student Government election held on 1 November 1984, with a revote the following week, filled congress seats rather than the presidency.
